Note::TexAccessor::strip_comments¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_comments() const

Remove TeX Comments Without Flattening Lines¶

strip_comments() removes an unescaped % and every following byte up to the next physical line ending. The line ending itself is retained. This makes it a source-cleaning step: line boundaries remain available to later diagnostics, paragraph handling, or fix_linebreaks(), while commented commands no longer participate in extraction and conversion.

A percent sign is escaped when immediately preceded by an odd run of backslashes; an even run leaves it active as a comment marker. LF, CRLF, and CR line endings are recognized independently and preserved byte-for-byte. A final comment without a line ending removes the remainder of that cell. The method is lexical: it does not attempt macro expansion or verbatim-environment parsing.

The transform is out-of-place, idempotent, shape preserving, and Text-only. Empty results remain empty strings in their original positions. Undefined state propagates, while defined non-Text Notes reject. Processing is one linear pass over each cell with one output allocation.

Example 1: Escapes And All Physical Line Endings¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    "keep \\% percent % LF\nnext",
    "alpha % CRLF\r\nbeta",
    "one % CR\rtwo",
    "100\\% visible"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_comments() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["keep \\% percent \nnext", "alpha \r\nbeta", "one \rtwo", "100\\% visible"]

Example 2: Comments Do Not Remove Matrix Lanes¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a % x\nb", "plain", "% all\nnext", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().strip_comments() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a \nb", "plain"],
  ["\nnext", ""]
]

Example 3: Idempotence, Undefined State, And Dtype¶

const auto once = pluss::make_note("a % hidden\nb").tex().strip_comments();
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent="
          << ((once == once.tex().strip_comments()).all().bool_item())
          << " undefined="
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_comments().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_comments();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

idempotent=true undefined=false
Int64: rejected
